items.title: v0.40.11
items.abstract_or_text: ## Speech Ollama can now generate [speech](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech) on macOS. `ollama run` plays text or a chat model's reply aloud as the audio is generated, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint. ```sh ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama." ``` ## d3 decision models [d3](https://ollama.com/library/d3) brings vLLM Semantic Router's decision models to Ollama. Give a model text, structured state, or an image, and ask it to classify, answer yes or no, or score options with probabilities. The family includes 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B sizes. ```sh ollama run d3 "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?" ``` ## New Contributors * @SynapShift made their first contribution in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19173 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.10...v0.40.11-rc0

items.abstract_or_text: Changes since langchain-core==1.6.13 release(core): 1.7.0 (#41418) feat(core): emit `tool-call-delta` for streamed tool-call args (#41257) ## Notes - Tool-call args now stream as `tool-call-delta` slices instead of `block-delta` snapshots of the args so far. If you read raw stream events and their `block-delta` args mid-stream, read `tool-call-delta` instead. `.tool_calls.get()` and `.output` are unchanged. To keep snapshots, pin `langchain-core<1.7`. - Since 1.6.13, iterating `ChatModelStream.tool_calls` yields each call's new args slice, not a snapshot of the args so far.

items.abstract_or_text: minimax-m3 : forward quant scales to the graph (fixes #31063) (#31097) The generic scale pass in llama-model.cpp loads the per-expert NVFP4 scale2 tensors (ffn_{up,gate,down}_exps_s) and the per-tensor MXFP8 scales for the dense FFN and the shared expert, but minimax-m3.cpp never forwarded any of them to the graph. build_moe_ffn() defaults these to nullptr, so build_lora_mm_id() skipped its w_s branch entirely and the routed-expert weights came out global_scale times too large, swamping the residual (reported G ~= 15123 for M3.1 Flash) and producing token soup. Forward all scale tensors at the three call sites, matching the pattern used by flint and the other NVFP4-capable MoE models. So when rejection sampling occurs it should still produce the same probability distribution as if we directly sampled from the target model. Running the test: ```console ctest --test-dir build -R "^test-speculative-rejection-sampling" \ --n_trials 5000 -V ``` This will generate two models, one target and one draft model. For subsequent runs use the "fixture exclude any" option to avoid recreating the models: ```console ctest --test-dir build-cpu-debug -R \ "^test-speculative-rejection-sampling" \ -FA "^speculative-models" --n_trails 5000 -V ``` * remove draft model **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: mtmd : lfm2 resize matches torchvision (#30943) * mtmd : lfm2 bilinear resize matches torchvision Lfm2VlImageProcessor and d1-omni vision.py resize uint8 images with torchvision (antialias=True). That is Pillow's algorithm, except that the weights are int16 with as many fractional bits as the largest weight allows, where Pillow uses 22 bits. The Pillow port was 1-2 levels off on about 1% of the values of the d1-omni and LFM2.5-VL crops. RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR_TORCH rounds the weights of the Pillow port to that precision and scales them back to 22 bits, which gives the output of torchvision with the same passes, and "bilinear" maps to it for LFM2 and d1-omni. Other models keep the Pillow algorithms. * mtmd : lfm2 bicubic resize matches torchvision Lfm2VlImageProcessor resizes with torchvision for the bicubic checkpoints too (d1-3B, LFM2-VL), so "bicubic" maps to RESIZE_ALGO_BICUBIC_TORCH for LFM2: the Pillow bicubic filter (a = -0.5, as torchvision with antialias) with the int16 weights of torchvision. The Pillow port was 1-2 levels off on about 0.25% of the values of the d1-3B crops. * use bitfield, add hparams setter --------- Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - items.abstract_or_text: hip: fix bf16 WMMA operand vector type for gfx11/gfx12 (#30885) The __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32 (and _gfx12) builtins take their A/B operands as vectors of short (_ExtVector / _ExtVector ), not __bf16. Declaring the fragments as ext_vector_type(N) __bf16 fails to compile: error: cannot initialize a parameter of type 'short __attribute__((ext_vector_type(16)))' with an lvalue of type 'const bf16x16_t' (vector of 16 '__bf16' values) short and __bf16 are both 16-bit and the value is only ever passed to the builtin via reinterpret_cast over raw bytes, so changing the element type is bit-identical. The operand type has been short since the builtin was introduced, so this works across LLVM/ROCm versions without a version gate. Fixes HIP builds for RDNA3 (gfx1150/1151) and RDNA4 (gfx1200/1201). items.abstract_or_text: Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored (#29864) * Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored Multi-column (2 to 80 activation columns) mul_mat_vec_q for reordered K-quant and Q8_0 weights on the Intel XMX matrix engines (int8 DPAS, ESIMD), for the SYCL backend. It targets speculative decoding verification (2 to 8 tokens per step) and short prompt batches (9 to 80 tokens). Three types also use it for a single column (Q2_K, Q3_K, Q8_0). * Fixed regression bug real bug found: the first version produced NaN whenever the row count wasn't a multiple of 4 * Removed GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 activation * rewritten xmx_mul_mat 64-byte alignment and 16-byte pitch check on the activations * Implemented fused gate/up kernel One launch computes up * act(gate) for both FFN weights, reading the activations once and applying SWIGLU or GEGLU in the epilogue. It covers up to 16 columns and works for all six XMX types. * Removed the temporary XMX_NOGLU environment switch * Q2_K min-sum optimization Q2_K weight is d·scl·q − dmin·mc, where scl (the 4-bit scale) and mc (the 4-bit min code) apply to each half of a 32-weight group * Added dispatch check and GRF sweep tg128 on Q4_K_M goes from 26.67 to 28.23 tok/s on the B70 (+5.9%). Q6_K is unchanged. MUL_MAT passes 1727/1727 and MUL_MAT_VEC_FUSION 1361/1361. Perplexity at batch 1 is 5.2064 with XMX and 5.2058 without. * Renamed variables * Added 2 environment variables GGML_SYCL_XMX_MAX_COLS (default 80, any value 0 or higher) and GGML_SYCL_XMX_GLU_MAX_COLS (default 16, range 0 to 16): the largest batch for the fused gate/up kernel. It is clamped to 16 because that is the most the fused kernel is compiled for, so the variable can only lower it. * Update esimd.hpp 1. All five quant structs were repeating the same boilerplate, so I moved it into shared pieces. 2. A new helper xmx_term does one DPAS, converts it to float and scales it per row. The four branches are now one or two lines each, and the shared Cb += z * d8r is written once. The refactor passes all three op tests.
